help.conn.transport: Auto: the CH340/CH343 serial port first, otherwise the paired Bluetooth device. A named port or device is used alone.
help.conn.settings: Volume and brightness are also set on the keyboard. Buttons stay off until the keyboard reports its settings.
help.conn.wifi.setup: Wi-Fi credentials go to the keyboard over USB only, and only while the pairing window is open. After it joins Wi-Fi, a SmartLife QR code appears here.
help.conn.unbind: For a new account or a fresh setup. This clears the keyboard's Wi-Fi and cloud binding. The Tuya UUID/AuthKey and the saved Wi-Fi list are kept. To change Wi-Fi only, use the Wi-Fi form.
help.conn.lic: The PID is written once over USB: the keyboard accepts it only while it has none, applies it after a restart, and it cannot be changed here afterwards. Without a PID the Tuya cloud stays off. Writes UUID and AuthKey to the keyboard over USB. The keyboard stores them, and Companion never keeps the secret. Read shows the UUID and the last four AuthKey characters.
help.ota: Installs a signed .akota package over USB. The keyboard checks the signature again and asks for K6 before it writes. Settings, keymap, pairing and the Tuya UUID/AuthKey are kept.
help.input.control: When on, board keys drive the local Kiro Crew window. When off, keys are only shown; PC actions and PC ASR stop too.
help.input.live: Each key lights while the board reports it pressed.
help.input.voice: Cloud ASR runs on the keyboard. PC recognition uses this PC's microphone, and the text comes back to the keyboard screen to confirm.
help.control.api: Companion talks to the local Kiro Crew gateway (127.0.0.1:5476) over REST and a WebSocket. Chats are identified by stable slot keys, so no window focus or Alt+N is needed.
help.control.keys: A, B and C are stable Kiro Crew chats. K1–K3 select the bound chat, and K5 submits. Pick a chat in the list, then long-press K1/K2/K3 to bind it.
help.control.watched: Watch pins the chat the keyboard screen mirrors. Following all shows the latest active chat.
help.control.legacy: Fallback path. It focuses the Kiro Crew window and types keys. Use it when the API is not reachable.

Any other chat uses keyboard mode: the words stay on the keyboard screen, K4 deletes (hold to clear), K6 sends them to the chat picked with K1–K3. PC mode needs keyboard control on and the Crew window; if it fails, the words go to the keyboard instead.

help.conn.ble: Bluetooth traffic is encrypted and authenticated with a key made on the keyboard. Pairing hands that key to this PC over USB only. Without it the keyboard ignores this PC over Bluetooth and sends it nothing. Pairing again replaces the key; clear the keyboard's copy with Settings → Device info, K1 twice, or with “Clear on the keyboard” here over USB (the keyboard asks for K6).
help.conn.voice: You can also switch on the keyboard (Settings → Voice mode). ASR types what you say into Kiro Crew. Chat talks to the Tuya agent: replies are spoken, shown on the keyboard and here, and never sent to Kiro Crew.

conn.wifi.title: Saved Wi-Fi
conn.wifi.waiting: Waiting for the keyboard to report its saved networks.

help.conn.wifi: The keyboard remembers up to 8 networks it connected to, including the one set up in the Tuya app. When the connection drops it scans and joins the strongest saved network, and when the list is full the one connected longest ago is replaced. Passwords stay on the keyboard and are never shown or sent. Deleting needs USB; deleting the network in use keeps the connection until it drops. Adding a network still goes through the Wi-Fi form with the pairing window open. You can also delete on the keyboard: Settings → Saved Wi-Fi, K6 twice. Ways to change network: a network it connected to before is rejoined by itself; for a new network, with USB use the Wi-Fi form here and the keyboard stays bound, without USB unbind the keyboard and pair it again in the Tuya app over Bluetooth, which clears the old binding. The Companion cannot write Wi-Fi over Bluetooth, for security.
